standard: All requested material parts, independently per answer. Grade the ruling, not support labels.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player chooses a color and puts that color's Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Each receives the Voting card set with that color on its backs, removes cards targeting colors not in play, and keeps their own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down into the center, keeping their values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: put each ID upright in its plastic stand; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center and keep values hidden.
grades.reason: Explicit upright stand and visible chosen-color ID, matching Voting cards, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained and hidden central4 deal.

grades.question: Is there a player-by-player voting turn order? When may a player change their face-down choice, and when are choices revealed?
grades.expected_answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
grades.observed_answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. After everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.question: In a seven-player vote, Red receives three votes, Blue two and Green two. Is a four-vote majority necessary to make Red a Target? Explain the Target threshold.
grades.expected_answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
grades.observed_answer: No four-vote majority is required. The player receiving the most votes is the Target; with Red at three and Blue and Green at two each, Red is the sole Target.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target.”
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.question: Red and Blue tie for the most votes. With neither playing Ambush, what happens to them, and may someone survive by having voted for either tied Target?
grades.expected_answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
grades.observed_answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement, subject to the Ambush rules.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; with tied Targets, voting for any one satisfies the voting requirement.
grades.reason: Correctly identifies both tied players as Targets and voting for either satisfies the requirement, but omits what happens to the Targets: both eliminated absent successful Ambush. Explicitly requested outcome remains missing; source-supported summary contains it, and no other answer may supply it.

grades.question: Blue is the sole Target. Green received no votes and voted for Red. Green did not Ambush. Does receiving no votes keep Green alive?
grades.expected_answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
grades.observed_answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, and did not play a successful Ambush. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception.
grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.question: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. How are votes tallied, who are the Targets, and who survives after Red's legal retaliation?
grades.expected_answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.observed_answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes, so Red contributes no vote; Yellow votes for Red and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives and may retaliate only against a player who voted for Red, which is Yellow. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
grades.reader_evidence: The three-player illustration states Red's Ambush is not a vote, Red and Yellow tie as Targets, Yellow is eliminated, Red may retaliate only against Yellow, and Pink survives after voting for tied Target Yellow.
grades.reason: Complete vote tally ignoring Ambush, Red/Yellow tied Targets, Red protected/retaliates on Yellow, and Pink survives for voting TargetYellow.

grades.question: A Target successfully plays Ambush and four players voted for them. Do they eliminate all four voters? May they choose a player who voted for another color instead?
grades.expected_answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
grades.observed_answer: No. A successful Ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate, even if four players voted for them. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: the successful ambusher chooses “one of the players who voted for them”; they cannot choose someone who voted for a different Target.
grades.reason: Restricts successful Ambush retaliation to exactly one voter who targeted the ambusher; rejects all-voter and arbitrary-color alternatives.

grades.question: A player chooses Ambush but is not among the Targets after the votes are counted. What happens to that player?
grades.expected_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.observed_answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only if its player is a Target; one played by someone who is not a Target fails and causes that player to self-eliminate.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”
grades.reason: Non-Target Ambush fails and self-eliminates.

grades.question: Four players survive a vote and its Ambush effects. Does the round award gold now, and who participates next?
grades.expected_answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
grades.observed_answer: The round does not award gold yet. With four survivors after the vote and Ambush effects, continue with another Conspire and vote among those survivors; eliminated players do not participate in later votes that round.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: with three or more survivors, continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.
grades.reason: Four survivors continue conspiracy/voting; no gold yet and only survivors vote.

grades.question: Exactly one player survives the round. What reward do they collect, and are the four cards four points?
grades.expected_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
grades.observed_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are cards whose values vary from 3 to 5 points each, not four points.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. Components: each bar is a card valued at 3, 4, or 5 points.
grades.reason: All four central cards awarded; values3/4/5points, not four points. No unsupported reveal-timing claim.

grades.question: Exactly two players survive the voting. What must they do, which cards does each receive, and how do they choose and reveal?
grades.expected_answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
grades.observed_answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down; when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously and apply the payoff table.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; each chooses one face down, and both choices are revealed simultaneously when both are ready.
grades.reason: Explicit Share/Steal/Grab One & Go set, discussion, secret face-down selection and simultaneous reveal.

grades.question: The final vote eliminates every participant. Who receives gold from the deck, who does not, and what happens to the four central bars for next round?
grades.expected_answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new bars; refill only enough to bring the pool to four.
grades.reader_evidence: For zero survivors: each player not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
grades.reason: Rewards only those absent from the final vote one deck card each; final voters receive none; all four central cards retained with no additions.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Share. How many Gold Bar cards does each receive?
grades.expected_answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”
grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Share and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
grades.observed_answer: The Steal player receives four central Gold Bar cards and the Share player receives none.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: Share gets 0 and Steal gets 4.
grades.reason: Steal takes all four, Share takes zero.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Steal player receives the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go versus Steal gives the Grab player 1 and the opponent 3; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar and the Share player receives the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Share versus Grab One & Go gives Share 3 and Grab One & Go 1.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two bars remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four, dealing them face down with values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: If both choose Grab One & Go, each receives one and the other two remain central; add just two new bars for the next round.
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one Gold Bar from the deck; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Check for victory at the end of a round after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. The threshold is at least 25 points with 6–9 players and at least 24 points with 10–12 players. If several qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: check at the end of a round after bars are awarded; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 players and 24 for 10–12; the highest point total wins.
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: The tied qualifying leaders conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. If there is no winner after a round, everyone returns and IDs are stood upright for another round.
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including texting and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: discussion lasts roughly a minute and a half at most; any method is allowed, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting; the game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; target using the card matching the player's visible ID color, or play Ambush to defend yourself.
grades.reason: Target-color Voting card placed face down in front of oneself; own Ambush replacement explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright so they are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: If the game continues after the entire pot is awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden. If bars remain central, deal only enough new face-down bars to bring the pool to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Refill the central pool to four as needed; deal new central bars face down with values hidden; after the entire pot is awarded deal four, or if bars remain add only enough to bring the pool to four.
grades.reason: Explicit four new central face-down hidden-value cards after full pot distribution; no requested preparation omitted.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. The Target is determined from the vote count, so Blue alone is the Target with four votes versus Purple's three. Blue's successful Ambush lets Blue survive but does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target and are eliminated unless a successful Ambush exception applies; Blue's survival alone does not let them survive.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: the player receiving the most votes is the Target; Ambush does not prevent another player from being a tied Target. Players who did not vote for any Target are eliminated, subject to successful Ambush.
grades.reason: Blue remains sole Target after successful protection; Purple not promoted; ordinary voters for Purple eliminated. Inapplicable generic Ambush caveat does not change actual ruling.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The tie instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among three or more tied players; that procedure is unsupported.

grades.reason: Both repeated-Showdown instruction and absence of multiway arrangement explicit. Source-limitation unsupported label is responsive to whether source specifies arrangement; same issue independently adjudicated in iteration02.

grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. In a double-Steal extra Showdown, each player outside the two finalists receives one Gold Bar card from the deck, and that reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner. Compare totals of all players at the table after each Showdown.
grades.reader_evidence: After each extra Showdown, compare totals of all players at the table; the one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
grades.reason: Explicit doubleSteal extra-Showdown one-deck-bar reward to every outsider and sole-highest outsider victory. No retraction about reward applicability.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; “If more than one player has reached the threshold, the highest point total wins.”
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: For exactly two qualifying players tied for the highest total, the booklet's instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total; one extra Showdown does not end the tie if the highest totals remain tied. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round; stand all IDs upright and begin another round.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied highest totals “conduct another Final Showdown” and “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: if no winner, “everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including speaking, whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; “Any method of communication is allowed, openly or secretly,” including “showing a Voting card, texting”; the game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target player's visible ID color and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself against being the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: use “the card matching that player's visible ID color”; each player places one card “face down in front of themselves”; to defend yourself, “play your Ambush card instead.”
grades.reason: Target-color Voting card placed face down in front of oneself; own Ambush replacement explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: Because all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down for the next round, keeping their values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Refill: “Deal new central bars face down, keeping their values hidden. If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.”
grades.reason: Explicit four new central face-down hidden-value cards after full pot distribution; no requested preparation omitted.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue has the most votes (four versus Purple's three), so Blue is the Target; Blue's successful Ambush protects Blue but does not change who had the most votes or make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target, so they are eliminated (unless protected by a successful Ambush exception).
grades.reader_evidence: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target”; a successful Ambush protects its Target, and “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.” Players who “did not vote for any Target” are eliminated.
grades.reason: Blue remains sole Target after successful protection; Purple not promoted; ordinary voters for Purple eliminated. Inapplicable generic Ambush caveat does not change actual ruling.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's tie instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as needed until there is a single player with the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Showdown among more than two tied leaders: the summary says the booklet's card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players, and provides no official multiway procedure.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring says tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown; source limitation says “its card sets, procedure, and payoff table cover only two players” and “provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.”
grades.reason: Both repeated-Showdown instruction and absence of multiway arrangement explicit. Source-limitation unsupported label is responsive to whether source specifies arrangement; same issue independently adjudicated in iteration02.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?

The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. In a double-Steal extra Showdown, every player outside the pair receives one Gold Bar from the deck. The summary expressly says this reward can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.
grades.reader_evidence: “The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.”
grades.reason: Explicit doubleSteal extra-Showdown one-deck-bar reward to every outsider and sole-highest outsider victory. No retraction about reward applicability.
